key_insight: Task-aware CT projection selection improves hemodynamic prediction under extreme sparsity, but projections optimized for this task can yield poor image reconstructions.
engineering_relevance: Sparse acquisition tailored to downstream flow quantities could reduce CT projection requirements without prioritizing image reconstruction quality.
method: Generate synthetic fan-beam CTA projections from CFD simulations of intracranial aneurysms.
Train a Fourier neural operator to predict spatially resolved and spatially averaged time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS).
Compare uniform and golden-angle sampling with Gumbel-Softmax, Soft top-K, and agentic AI selection across view budgets.
evidence_signal: On synthetic CTA data, agentic AI and Soft top-K achieved the lowest mean errors for spatially resolved TAWSS, with agentic AI slightly better; optimized selection mattered most at extreme sparsity.
watch_item: Validation on synthetic projections does not establish robustness to clinical CT noise, acquisition artifacts, or patient variability.
paper_title: Agentic AI Reasoning and Learned Sampling for Task-Aware Projection Selection in Sparse-View CT: Predicting Hemodynamics
